The previous attempt named no dataset (reason given: I could not confirm any public dataset, with a verified landing page or DOI, that records floret or seed centre coordinates, or parastichy crossing angles, for sunflower capitula. GBIF, NCBI, Dryad and similar portals hold occurrence, genome and trait data, not per-capitulum floret geometry. Citing a specific paper's supplement from memory would risk a fabricated identifier, so I return null. The test would need either a new image set of sunflower heads with floret coordinates extracted, or a published coordinate dataset that I have not verified.).

The previous attempt named no dataset (reason given: I could not find a public dataset with a verified landing page or DOI that records per-floret centre coordinates or parastichy crossing angles for sunflower capitula. A search of the open portals found only related items. Swinton's arXiv paper 2407.05857 (Disk-stacking models are consistent with Fibonacci and non-Fibonacci structure in sunflowers) refers to a large dataset of seedheads, but its arXiv page gives no repository, no dataset DOI and no URL, and it describes parastichy counts rather than coordinates or angles. Parastichy counts alone cannot decide a test about crossing angles. The capitulum-inclination record on data.gov is about head tilt, not floret positions. Naming any of these as the dataset would misrepresent it, and I will not guess at a supplement from memory. The test needs a new set of sunflower head images with floret centres extracted, or a published coordinate set that I have not verified.).

I am leaving the dataset null rather than risk an invented identifier.).
